job_24c7e48608af602a: Assistant Professor or Associate Professor in Lithospheric DeformationApply now DescriptionThe Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences (EPS) at The University of Texas at Austin (UT) seeks to hire an Assistant Professor (tenure-track) or Associate Professor (tenured) in the field of Lithospheric Deformation. job_337a46a6f0f01296: Assistant, Associate or Full Professor without tenure, UW Pediatrics Rheumatology Division Position Overview School / Campus / College: School of Medicine Organization: Pediatrics, Rheumatology Title: Assistant, Associate or Full Professor without tenure, UW Pediatrics Rheumatology Division Position Details Position Description The Division of Rheumatology, in the Department of Pediatrics, at the University of Washington, is seeking candidates for a full-time position at the level of Assistant Professor (without tenure by reason of funding), Associate Professor (without tenure by reason of funding), or full Professor (without tenure by reason of funding) on the Clinician-Scholar track. Rank is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Anticipated start date is winter 2026. Assistant Professors are eligible for multi-year appointments that align with a 12-month service period (July 1-June 30). Faculty with 12-month service periods are paid for 11 months of service over a 12-month period (July-June), meaning the equivalent of one month is available for paid time off. Associate and full Professors hold indefinite appointments that align with a 12-month service period (July 1-June 30). Faculty with 12-month service periods are paid for 11 months of service over a 12-month period (July-June), meaning the equivalent of one month is available for paid time off. All University of Washington faculty engage in teaching, research and service. The faculty member will engage in pediatric rheumatology clinical care in the outpatient, inpatient, and outreach settings, as well as immunosuppressive medication management and intraarticular aspirations/injections. The successful candidate will spend 80% time in the clinical setting and 20% time in administrative and scholarly pursuit including teaching and mentoring. Clinical effort may be reduced, commensurate with grant funding. As the second largest Department in the UW School of Medicine, Pediatrics has twenty-one clinical divisions with approximately 1,400 academic appointments, including approximately 650 paid faculty members, 134 residents, 70 ACGME fellows, 230 staff employees and over 600 volunteer/affiliate faculty and continues to grow each year. The Department of Pediatrics is a close affiliate of Seattle Children's Hospital (SCH) and Seattle Children's Research Institute (SCRI). Faculty members appointed in the Department are located at various institutions (including Seattle Children’s, UW Medicine, and FHCRC), and are part of the Children’s University Medical Group (CUMG) clinical practice plan. The Division of Rheumatology, at Seattle Children’s Hospital and Research Institute and the University of Washington, is world-renowned as one of the oldest programs in the world and is the largest in the United States – with 13 physicians and 4 nurses that serve the states of Washington, Alaska, and Idaho. Our diverse population of patients come primarily from these states, and represents a wide range of ethnicities and backgrounds as well as unique and rare diseases. Community members make up and continue to make up much of the faculty search committee tasked with hiring the best public health researchers in the country to address these issues. Position description The Department of Neurobiology at the David Geffen School of Medicine (DGSOM) at UCLA invites applications for an open-rank tenure-track/tenured faculty position. We welcome applications from candidates at all levels whose research addresses fundamental questions in neuroscience or explores mechanisms of disease. The ideal candidate will pursue interdisciplinary approaches to address major unanswered questions about the nervous system. We encourage applications from investigators working across a broad range of scales - including genetics, molecular neuroscience, systems/circuit neuroscience, computation, behavior and cognition. Applicants must hold a Ph.D. and/or M.D. (or equivalent degree) in a neuroscience-related field. Preference will be given to early-career candidates at the Assistant Professor level; however, exceptional candidates at the Associate Professor or Full Professor level will be considered. Evaluation of applicants will emphasize research accomplishments and creativity, teaching excellence, professional contributions, and service to the academic community. We also seek candidates who demonstrate a commitment to fostering a positive and inclusive academic environment. The successful candidate will be expected to maintain an active and innovative research program and contribute to mentoring and training activities at UCLA. Teaching and service responsibilities will be consistent with those of other tenure-track/tenured faculty members in the DGSOM. UCLA offers competitive salaries, research start-up support, recruitment resources, state-of-the-art modern laboratories, computing resources and research infrastructure, as well as a vibrant community of collaborative scholars. The Department of Neurobiology is a leading center for neuroscience research and education at UCLA, with faculty research spanning a wide range of neuroscience disciplines, methodologies, experimental systems, and levels of analysis. The department is part of the DGSOM, one of the top medical schools in the US, and is affiliated with one of the nation’s pre-eminent health systems. job_e8657c41e62da9b8: Postdoctoral Scholar-Fixed Term East Lansing, Michigan, United States Fisheries And Wildlife 10002344 Area of Interest: Research/Scientific Full Time/Part Time: Full Time (90-100%) Group: Fixed Term Academic Staff Remote Work: Remote-Friendly Union/Non-Union: Non-Union Show More Show Less Faculty/Academic Staff Opening on: Jul 22 2026 Closing at: Jul 22 2028 - 23:55 EDT 55598.00-60000.00 Salary Commensurate with Experience College Of Agriculture And Nat Resources 1144260 View favorites Position Summary The Michigan Department of Natural Resources (DNR), Wildlife Division, and conservation partners operating in Michigan need a planning document and interactive tool that identifies both priority locations for restoring wetlands and conserving existing wetlands in the context of waterfowl habitat and related ecosystem functions and services. Historically, waterfowl and wetland staff within Wildlife Division have drafted and updated a statewide strategic document outlining where to focus wetland conservation efforts based on physiographic regions and migratory pathways to implement the North American Waterfowl Management Plan (NAWMP) habitat conservation goals. Michigan DNR, Wildlife Division, and partners need updated strategic guidance identifying locations and hotspots that can guide on-the-ground conservation delivery for waterfowl, other wetland wildlife, and societal benefit. The selected candidate will be a member of the U.S. Geological Survey’s Michigan Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit under the direction of unit scientists. The unit is housed in the Department of Fisheries and Wildlife at Michigan State University. The position has secured funding support for ~2 years. The goal of this project is to design and develop spatially explicit decision support tools and assist with updating an Implementation Plan to identify and prioritize locations in Michigan which are most suitable to protect and restore for waterfowl and wetland associated functions and services. This goal will be achieved by fulfilling the following objectives: Convening of conservation partners To convene conservation partners with an interest in waterfowl habitat conservation in Michigan and facilitate the gathering of knowledge, data, and input on habitat objectives, priorities, and modeling. Geospatial modeling To model the spatial distribution and quantify the suitability of waterfowl habitat conservation capital and opportunity in Michigan, including consideration and modeling of associated environmental and social factors. Strategy drafting To lead the development of a draft Michigan waterfowl habitat conservation strategy which defines and assesses progress towards habitat restoration and retention objectives, considers historical population dynamics and landscape changes, guides spatial prioritization and evaluation of habitat delivery, evaluates multiple conservation benefits (e.g., ecosystem goods and services), and recommends monitoring and research priorities. Interactive online geospatial interface To design online spatially explicit decision support tools for waterfowl habitat conservation in Michigan. This objective includes the following sub-objective: To provide all datasets and associated codebooks including all variables and equations, documentation of any weighting and imputation procedures as relevant, any associated survey or interview instruments, and documentation of any models including all equations and a discussion of all assumptions. Datasets and models will be in format compatible with Wildlife Division software and hardware.
